## Trial `cron-access-control-rhel9__f7tVagz`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The task — restricting cron scheduling on node1 to root and opsadmin — is fully and directly satisfied. The executor created the missing opsadmin account, wrote /etc/cron.allow with exactly root and opsadmin, removed the conflicting empty /etc/cron.deny, and proved enforcement both positively (root and opsadmin can create/list crontabs) and negatively (a third test account was denied with the expected cronie error). Test artifacts (testuser, temp crontabs) were fully cleaned up, leaving only the intended configuration, confirmed by a final check. The executor additionally ran the required independent node-restart evidence protocol: a pre-restart healthy baseline, a backgrounded reboot with immediate acknowledgement, a directly observed boot-id change after the connection dropped and recovered, and confirmation that crond, cron.allow, and opsadmin's cron access all survived the reboot. Hygiene is clean; the only residue is a harmless /tmp/reboot.log from the shutdown command.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. All state-changing commands trace clearly to satisfying the task or the independent restart protocol: creating opsadmin (required by the task), creating/removing a temporary testuser and test crontabs (needed to prove enforcement, fully reverted via crontab -r, loginctl terminate-user, pkill, userdel -r), writing /etc/cron.allow and removing /etc/cron.deny (the core task change), and the single bounded reboot (independent protocol requirement, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect). The after-prepare vs after-executor diff shows only the expected boot-id change, ephemeral systemd-private temp dirs regenerated per-boot, sshd/chronyd re-listening with new PIDs after reboot, and one new file /tmp/reboot.log (harmless shutdown-command log, low-risk residue). No failed services, no package-health regressions, and no orphaned test accounts or crontabs remained.
